data.gist: Limitations: small animal numbers (4-week OARSI only trended), single injection at a single time point, single human donor for both products, and author ties to the BMAX company, mitigated by blinding and independent site.
data.plain: The authors list constraints: few animals, so some outcomes only trended (cartilage scores were significant at 8 weeks but not 4); treatment was given once, 4 weeks after surgery, with no other timings or repeat dosing tested; and both products came from one human donor, so donor variability in MSC content and matrix composition limits generalizability. They also disclose that some co-authors have relationships with the BMAX developer, noting the animal work was done at an independent institution with a conflict-free injecting surgeon and blinded assessors, but say external validation is still needed. They maintain that within these conditions the ECM-retaining product consistently outperformed BMAC.
